statement: PROOF FOR THE EXPLICIT FAMILY; independent audit pending. For rate-one continuous-time simple random walk on G_d=(Z/2Z)^d x Z/m_dZ, m_d=max(2,floor(2^d log(d)/4)), with generators (e_i,a) for a!=0 and (h,0) for h!=0, the spectral gap is asymptotic to 2/d, t_mix(1/4) is asymptotic to d log(d)/4, and t_mix(3/4)/t_mix(1/4) tends to log(4/3). Thus this simple unweighted Abelian Cayley family satisfies the spectral product condition and lacks total-variation cutoff. This reconstructs an existing campaign candidate; no priority claim or audited solution of the literature question is made.
assumptions: Exact generator set and auxiliary group as stated

statement: PROOF OF A SPECIAL CASE; independent audit pending. Fix a,b in [0,1] and let K(z)=[[a,z],[conjugate(z),b]]. On the disk |z|^2<=min(ab,(1-a)(1-b)), the Shannon entropy of the determinantal subset measure with kernel K(z) is concave as a function of the complex number z. Its four atom probabilities are ab-|z|^2, (1-a)(1-b)-|z|^2, a(1-b)+|z|^2, and (1-a)b+|z|^2. This covers all two-site Hermitian positive contractions with common diagonals, including boundary kernels, but does not settle jointly varying diagonals or larger kernels.
assumptions: The two diagonal entries are held fixed

statement: PROOF OF THE STATED SCOPED RESULT; independent audit pending. If Shannon entropy of finite determinantal measures is midpoint-concave in the positive-contraction kernel for every finite set, then the entropy rate of stationary determinantal processes on Z is midpoint-concave in their measurable [0,1]-valued circle symbols. Finite restrictions are linear in the symbol; dividing their inequalities by the interval length and taking the subadditive entropy-rate limit proves the implication. No converse is asserted, and the fixed-diagonal two-site lemma does not supply the premise for all sizes.
assumptions: Finite-kernel concavity is assumed at every size
Stationary binary determinantal processes with symbols in [0,1]

statement: PROOF OF THE STATED SCOPED RESULT; independent audit pending. For an increasing deterministic sequence T_m asymptotic to m^2 log(m), the generalized inverse max{m:T_m<=t} is asymptotic to sqrt(2t/log(t)). It is not asymptotic to sqrt(t)/log(t). This corrects an arithmetic implication in C0135-A001; it does not assert that the excited-walk clock has the assumed asymptotic behavior.

PROOF OF THE STATED SCOPED RESULT; independent audit pending. Let S_k=max_{j<=k} X_j and a_n=sqrt(n) log(n). If for every finite T, max_{k<=floor(nT)} |S_k-X_k|/a_n tends to zero in probability, and S_floor(nt)/a_n converges in the Skorokhod J1 topology to a continuous process Y, then X_floor(nt)/a_n also converges to Y. The identity time change bounds their J1 distance by the displayed uniform norm. A uniform O_P(sqrt(n)) backtracking estimate suffices; a fixed-time estimate alone does not establish this hypothesis. No such estimate under the weaker ERW cookie assumptions is claimed.
assumptions: Uniform backtracking hypothesis on every compact time interval
Continuous J1 limit of the rescaled maximum

statement: PROOF OF THE STATED SCOPED RESULT; independent audit pending. Let G be a countable connected graph of maximum degree Delta>=2 with iid finite nonnegative edge weights W. If for some theta>0, (Delta-1) E exp(-theta W)<1, then almost surely every vertex pair has a finite path attaining its passage-time infimum. Counting simple paths, exponential Markov bounds and Borel-Cantelli make all bounded-cost competitors have bounded lengths. In particular (Delta-1)P(W=0)<1 suffices, even without a positive lower bound or a finite mean. On Z^d this gives the known sufficient subrange P(W=0)<1/(2d-1), leaving the arbitrary-law question unresolved.
assumptions: Countable connected locally finite graph of maximum degree Delta>=2

statement: PROOF OF THE STATED SCOPED RESULT; independent audit pending. Consider one FCFS server with Poisson arrival rate lambda>0 and independent exponential service rate mu>lambda. After becoming empty it remains on for deterministic grace g in [0,infinity], then switches off. A cold arrival triggers deterministic setup tau>=0, which is never cancelled; arrivals during setup wait. Put p=exp(-lambda g), x=lambda tau, rho=lambda/mu and y=p/(1+xp), with p=0 at g=infinity. The stationary mean queueing wait is lambda/[mu(mu-lambda)] + tau(1+x/2)y. If busy, on-idle, off and setup powers are B,I,O,U, average power is rho B+(1-rho)I+(1-rho)[O+xU-(1+x)I]y. Hence varying the grace period traces an affine waiting-power curve. The formula includes arrivals during setup and the subsequent busy period. It addresses k=1 and does not claim the many-server frontier or optimality among other policies.
assumptions: Deterministic nonnegative setup tau and grace g
Setup is never cancelled; setup arrivals queue

statement: PROOF OF THE STATED SCOPED RESULT; independent audit pending. Consider one FCFS server with Poisson arrival rate lambda>0 and independent exponential service rate mu>lambda. After becoming empty it remains on for deterministic grace g in [0,infinity], then switches off. A cold arrival triggers deterministic setup tau>=0, which is never cancelled; arrivals during setup wait. Set p=exp(-lambda g), x=lambda tau and rho=lambda/mu. Busy, on-idle, off and setup occupy fractions rho, (1-rho)(1-p)/(1+xp), (1-rho)p/(1+xp), and (1-rho)xp/(1+xp). A cycle from one empty epoch to the next has expected duration mu/[lambda(mu-lambda)](1+xp). These fractions sum to one and include all setup arrivals.
assumptions: Deterministic nonnegative setup tau and grace g
Setup is never cancelled; setup arrivals queue

statement: PROOF OF THE STATED SCOPED RESULT; independent audit pending. For a continuous-time birth-death queue with birth rate lambda, death rate mu>lambda, killed on hitting zero, the expected busy duration from k>=0 is k/(mu-lambda) and the expected integral of queue length before extinction is k^2/[2(mu-lambda)]+(lambda+mu)k/[2(mu-lambda)^2]. The quadratic function has generator equal to minus k; negative drift gives exponential jump-count tails, which justify stopping and passage to the limit. These identities also average over a Poisson initial queue.
assumptions: Kill the process on hitting zero

statement: PROOF OF THE STATED SCOPED RESULT; independent audit pending. For a nearest-neighbour walk on Z^d with iid increments and mean e1 drift u>0, starting at zero, stop at longitudinal +/-L or transverse distance L^3. For some theta>0 and all sufficiently large integer L, the chance of exiting anywhere but the +L face is at most exp(-theta L)+exp(-u^2(L^3-1)/8), and hence below L^(-M) for every fixed M at large L. An exponential supermartingale handles backward exit; bounded iid increments and Hoeffding handle the delayed forward hit. The proof requires iid increments and does not infer the analogous bound from annealed velocity in a general random environment.
assumptions: Start at zero; boxes and stopping rule as stated

statement: PROOF OF THE STATED SCOPED RESULT; independent audit pending. For integer d>=2 let a_d=1-1/d and F_d(z)=[(1-z)^(-1)+exp(-d)(1-z/a_d)^(-1)]/[1+exp(-d)]. Its Taylor coefficients are nonnegative, F_d(0)=1, and its first pole is a_d. On every fixed [0,1-epsilon], |F_d(z)-(1-z)^(-1)|<=3 exp(-d)/epsilon for all large d, giving the same asymptotic expansion to every order in 1/d, yet its first pole is shifted by 1/d. Thus compact subcritical expansions alone cannot locate a critical point; the lace-free susceptibility route requires additional control near criticality or exclusion of small-residue poles. This is an analytic countermodel to an inference, not a percolation counterexample.
assumptions: Specified analytic family, not an asserted susceptibility law
Fixed compact intervals strictly below one

statement: PROOF OF THE STATED SCOPED RESULT; independent audit pending. For a deterministic K=1 NK-form landscape on 2m bits with F(x)=sum_i J_i 1{x_(2i-1)=x_(2i)}, J_i>0, there are 2^m strict single-bit local maxima, all global. Two distinct peaks differing on pair set D connect by a single-bit path inside {F>=max F-delta} exactly when delta>=max_{i in D} J_i. Every level-set component contains a peak and the component count is 2^(number of J_i>delta). For J_i=1, all peaks are isolated below deficit one and the whole level set is connected at deficit one. This is a deterministic block model, not the typical iid Gaussian NK model with overlapping neighborhoods.

PROOF OF THE STATED SCOPED RESULT; independent audit pending. For integer r>=2 and p in [2,infinity], diagonal real order-r multilinear tensors T_i and independent standard g_i, if p<=r then E||sum g_i T_i||_(I_p)<=sqrt(2 log(2d)) sqrt(sum ||T_i||_(I_p)^2). For p>r set q=p/(p-r), q=1 at p=infinity. If q>=2 the same bound holds with constant c_q=(E|g|^q)^(1/q) and no dimension factor; if 1<=q<2 it holds with factor d^(1/q-1/2)=d^(1/2-r/p). These bounds also hold for diagonal homogeneous polynomial norms, multiplying by at most 2^(1/q) for even r and p>r. They imply the proposed d^(1/2-1/p) scale on this diagonal family, up to the stated logarithm and constants. Off-diagonal tensors remain unresolved.
assumptions: Independent standard coefficient Gaussians; coordinate Gaussians may be correlated
Use the stated multilinear or polynomial norm convention

statement: PROOF OF THE STATED SCOPED RESULT; independent audit pending. Let T_a(x1,...,xr)=sum_j a_j product_k xk_j, with every xk in the l_p unit ball. Its multilinear norm is ||a||_infinity for p<=r and ||a||_q for p>r, q=p/(p-r), with q=1 at p=infinity. For the homogeneous polynomial using one repeated vector, the same identities hold for p<=r and for odd r. For even r and p>r the polynomial norm is max(||a_+||_q,||a_-||_q), so it is within factor 2^(1/q) of the multilinear norm. Explicit Holder optimizers prove all identities; the mixed-sign example r=2,p=infinity,a=(1,-1) has norms two and one.
assumptions: Independent standard coefficient Gaussians; coordinate Gaussians may be correlated

statement: PROOF OF THE STATED SCOPED RESULT; independent audit pending. Let an infinite connected locally finite unit-conductance graph C contain a subdivision of a locally finite graph H, replacing each edge e by an internally vertex-disjoint path of length ell_e. If H has a unit flow f from a root to infinity with sum_e ell_e f(e)^2 finite, then C is transient. Lift the constant current along each replacement path; its energy is exactly that sum and its divergence is inherited at branch vertices. Uniformly bounded corridor lengths suffice whenever H is transient. A percolation argument must establish this quantitative energy condition, not only branching topology.
assumptions: An actual subdivision with disjoint path interiors
A specified root-to-infinity unit flow with finite weighted energy

statement: PROOF OF THE STATED SCOPED RESULT; independent audit pending. In a rooted binary tree whose edges between levels k-1 and k are replaced by paths of integer length ell_k>=1 and unit conductance, resistance from the root to infinity equals sum_{k>=1} ell_k/2^k. Equal current splitting attains this energy and Cauchy-Schwarz on each level gives the matching lower bound. Thus ell_k=k is transient with resistance two, while ell_k=2^k is recurrent. An infinite binary branching topology alone does not guarantee transience after stretching.
assumptions: Exactly a level-subdivided rooted binary tree
